To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have developed a fast algorithm for scheduling instructions with time-constrained on pipelined machines, and (2), the algorithm is applicable to a class of instances that includes precedence constraints and release-times.

we present the first algorithm for scheduling unit execution time instructions on multiple pipelines with release times and deadlines that runs in time O((n)3/α(n)), where α(n) is the functional invers of the Ackermann Function.
we provide the theoretical basis for scheduling time-constraints on processors with ILPs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
scheduling instructions on pipelined machines.
developing a fast algorithm for scheduling unit execution time instructions on processors with multiple pipelines, precedence constraints and time-constraints.
developing a theoretical framework for instruction scheduling with time-constraints and precedence constraints on pipelined machines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the scheduling algorithm presented in this paper is optimal in the sense that it runs in time O(1.618/sup n/).

our algorithm is a practical and provably optimal solution for scheduling basic-block instructions with time-constrained instructions in the presence of release times, deadlines, and arbitrary latencies.

the problem of scheduling unit-execution time instructions on processors with pipelining in the presence of time constraints is NP-complete and that our algorithm is the first polynomial time algorithm to solve the problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a polynomial time algorithm that can be applied to all of the cases where the previously known algorithms are polynomial time.
we have provided the theoretical foundation for instruction scheduling with deadlines, latencies and precedence constraints, and have developed an algorithm with provable performance guarantees.

, we have extended the theoretical foundations of instruction scheduling to the presence of time-constraints, and have provided an algorithm for the first time for scheduling unit-executed-time instructions in the presence of time constraints.
The main takeaway from our work is that
scheduling unit-execution time instructions with time-constraint is NP-hard, but can be solved efficiently.

the theoretical foundations of instruction scheduling can be extended to handle more complex constraints, and can provide insights for the design of efficient heuristic algorithms for instruction scheduling.
the scheduling problem for basic-blocks of time-constrained instructions is tractable for a large class of instances.
